name: Single-generalist (no-latent) baseline evaluation
authority: PI, 2026-09-03, closing the flagged-but-unfilled gap recorded in artifacts/strategic_demand/sappo_crossover/summary.json: "pi_G was NOT continued under SAPPO, so it has no counterpart here. R3 remains gated behind this test."
QUESTION: Do we actually need latent specialization at all? If a single policy trained across the mixed opponent distribution, with no strategic-mode mechanism, matches the latent system's crossover, the latent mechanism needs a more careful justification. If it does not, that is direct evidence the latent mechanism is doing real work.

MODEL_UNDER_TEST.verified_architecture: latent_k=0, uses_latent_strategy=False -- confirmed by LOADING the checkpoint and inspecting the real model object, not by trusting its run_config.json (whose resolved_ppo_config reports latent_k=4, an inherited-but-inert field from the shared G0-V5 base config this run's own docstring calls a 'non-latent DIAGNOSTIC gate'; the loaded model's actual attributes are the ground truth used here).
MODEL_UNDER_TEST.training_opponent_pool: OP6 + OP7, weights (0.5, 0.5) -- the mixed distribution, per experiments/run_r1_repertoire_training.py:POLICIES['G']
MODEL_UNDER_TEST.no_training_or_tuning_here: this checkpoint is used strictly as-is, inference only. No fine-tuning, no additional steps, no architecture change.

PROTOCOL.reused_not_new: this is the SAME sealed block RSCFT's EVAL used, reused deliberately for direct pairing against whichever latent-system result is designated the paper's final comparison target. Reusing an already-opened seed range for a DIFFERENT, never-before-evaluated checkpoint does not reopen or contaminate RSCFT's own one-shot result -- the one-shot rule protects against re-scoring RSCFT's OWN arms on these seeds, not against a distinct model being scored on them once.
PROTOCOL.no_z_conditioning: pi_G is evaluated with no fixed_latent_strategy call at all -- the model does not condition on z, verified empirically before this spec was frozen
PROTOCOL.metric: win rate (binary), identical convention to every crossover measurement in this program
PROTOCOL.bootstrap: paired percentile bootstrap, seed as the resampling unit, n_boot=20000, alpha=0.05, rng_seed=7 -- reuses eval_hog_psp_v3._mean_ci unchanged

COMPARISON_RULE.definition: Delta_G_A = V(z0,A) - V(pi_G,A),   Delta_G_B = V(z1,B) - V(pi_G,B)
COMPARISON_RULE.target_latent_result: whichever result file is designated the paper's final champion (RSCFT_EVAL_RESULT.json's TREATMENT arm if it passes the primary gate; else a separate PI decision) -- NOT fixed in this spec, because the champion is not yet known. The comparison script reads it as an explicit argument, not a guess.
COMPARISON_RULE.desired_outcome: z0@A > pi_G@A AND z1@B > pi_G@B, with LCB95(Delta_G_A) > 0 and LCB95(Delta_G_B) > 0
COMPARISON_RULE.if_pi_G_matches_or_beats_the_latent_syst: report it as such. The reviewer's question is then legitimate, and the latent mechanism needs a more careful justification in Discussion/Limitations -- this is NOT a result to omit or reframe.

TIE_OR_REVERSAL: if the comparison is a tie or reversal on either pole (Delta_G <= 0), the same row-level integrity audit rule this program has held every prior EVAL to applies: a row-level audit is required, written before its rows are read, before any interpretation.
ORDER: finish sealed RSCFT EVAL -> freeze this spec (done, this file) -> build eval_pi_g.py (done, not yet run) -> run the 128-episode pi_G evaluation -> run the comparison against whichever latent result is designated final
one_shot: pi_G's EVAL runs exactly once, no rerun under any outcome
no_post_hoc_thresholds: the comparison rule above is exactly as frozen; it is not adjustable after pi_G's numbers are seen
DO_NOT_RUN_UNTIL: the RSCFT sealed EVAL (11704001..11704064) has fully completed. Running pi_G's evaluation concurrently would contend for the same GPU and seed-block attention as the still-open RSCFT result.
